Text: So  if you'll allow me a few minutes, I thought I would take the opportunity to sort of describe for the public  Claremont's development authority and its role in the context of the city's economic development efforts. And from time to time, there are questions that have come up about that, how the CDA fits alongside the  city management and  economic development efforts.

Speaker: Speaker 3
Text: And those are fair questions. So  let me just start by saying that Claremont's development authority is one of a few that are  established around the state. Ours was established in 1989 under state statute RSA 162 G  as the Claremont Industrial Authority and adopted by the City Council. Development authorities exist as a tool that a city or town can use to help implement economic development projects, particularly those involving real estate financing or longer timelines.

Speaker: Speaker 3
Text: A development authority does not replace  the city's economic development office, nor does it have powers the city itself doesn't already have. The city can take on the same underlying activities, such as committing to development projects, purchasing property, accessing grants and the development authority remains under city oversight. What it can provide is additional bandwidth,  a structure that the city can use to  if  when projects benefit from flexibility, from continuity over longer timelines, specialized financing, property management issues, or things that communities without a development authority might have less bandwidth to do  but could still do.

Speaker: Speaker 3
Text: Claremont Development Authority in its current form, was developed under the San Diego administration in 2003, when the previous Industrial Development Authority was reorganized from a 15 member body into a nine member board and placed under the administration directly through the city's Economic Development Director.  Its bylaws, updated in 2024  and adopted by the council, still reflect that design, and since that redesign, the CD-Rs generally been used to help execute projects identified through the city's economic development efforts, which in the past and should in the future align with priorities of city management, the Council, and informed by the Master plan.

Speaker: Speaker 3
Text: Current bylaws reflect this relationship. Our state that the  CDA is to act in concert with the city of  City of Claremont's Economic Development Office, and that the city's economic development director serves as the administrator for the CDA.  The types of tools a development authority can provide subject to city oversight include buying and holding development related real estate over longer timelines, structuring financing packages that may involve grants, loans or layered financing.

Speaker: Speaker 3
Text: Support for redevelopment or mixed use projects requiring coordination with private partners, and helping  with continuity for projects that may take several years to bring to completion.
